# Architecture

* [Packaging three.js as a desktop and iPad app](desktop-and-ipad-packaging.md) - The owner targets a native desktop and iPad app on three.js. The research covered Electron (fixed Chromium 152), Tauri (system webview, WKWebView on macOS and iOS) and PWAs; Electron does not reach iPad, so the iPad route is an open question.

# Catalog

* [Engine licence and running costs](licence-and-running-costs.md) - Licence terms per option (three.js and the web stack free and permissive; Unreal 5% royalty; Unity US$2,310-4,950 per seat plus ~4% for Industry; Omniverse free; Qt Quick 3D GPLv3 or commercial) and the backend a design tool implies; the real cost difference is engineering time.

# Component

* [Babylon.js](babylonjs.md) - Status FALLBACK (named by the research, not re-evaluated by the owner). Apache-2.0, 9.30 (Oct 2026), WebGPU labelled complete, no breaking changes flagged, more editor tools in core, Adobe-contributed OpenPBR; weaker for custom BRDFs (fragile shader injection) and for constantly edited instance sets.
* [Google Filament](filament.md) - Status NOT CHOSEN. Apache-2.0 PBR renderer (v1.78, Oct 2026) with the most fabric-specific built-in shading (cloth model, sheen, anisotropy, clear coat, iridescence since Sept 2026) on Windows, macOS, iOS/iPadOS, Android, Linux and WebGL 2; renderer only, offline material compiler, stale npm package.
* [Godot](godot.md) - Status NOT CHOSEN. MIT, no fees, 4.7 (June 2026) with area lights, HDR output, a per-light custom BRDF hook, pen pressure and a proven tool UI (Material Maker, Pixelorama, Xogot on iPad); but no sheen or iridescence, no OIT, no documented ray tracing, and web export is WebGL 2 only.
* [Hand-rolled renderer (and when it becomes justified)](hand-rolled-renderer.md) - Status NOT NOW; second fallback. Writing our own WebGPU/native renderer buys total control of the lighting loop, transparency and bundle size, but means rebuilding infrastructure engines already ship (pipeline caching, device loss, fallbacks); justified only if an engine demonstrably blocks the sparkle pipeline or speed target.
* [Native graphics libraries and application frameworks](native-small-libraries.md) - Status NOT CHOSEN; reference for a native fallback. The middle ground between an engine and raw graphics APIs: bgfx, Diligent, The Forge, Dawn, wgpu and Bevy for rendering; Qt (and Qt Quick 3D), Dear ImGui and egui for the application shell; plus web thin layers (TypeGPU, luma.gl).
* [NVIDIA Omniverse and OpenUSD](omniverse-and-openusd.md) - Status REJECTED on hardware grounds. Omniverse Kit gives turn-key RTX path tracing and is free for production since May 2026, but requires a GeForce RTX 3070 on Windows or Ubuntu with no macOS or iPad; OpenUSD remains plausible as an export format.
* [PlayCanvas](playcanvas.md) - Status NOT CHOSEN. MIT engine 2.23 (Oct 2026), WebGL2-first with WebGPU labelled beta; glTF-level materials, strong editor classes (picker, gizmos, outline), but custom shading needs paired GLSL and WGSL chunk overrides, compute and indirect draws are WebGPU-only, and its 2026 focus is Gaussian splats.
* [three.js editor ecosystem](threejs-editor-ecosystem.md) - Libraries around three.js that an editor needs: three-mesh-bvh for picking and painting, three-gpu-pathtracer for a final-quality still mode, react-three-fiber and drei (WebGPU support still alpha), pmndrs postprocessing (WebGL-only stable), and model-viewer.
* [three.js WebGPU renderer maturity and upgrade risk](threejs-renderer-maturity.md) - three.js's own manual calls WebGPURenderer experimental, nearly every release has breaking changes and deprecations last 10 releases; Spline v2 nonetheless ships on it with a WebGL build alongside. Mitigation: pin versions, upgrade in steps, keep a WebGL 2 path.
* [three.js (chosen engine)](threejs.md) - Status CHOSEN. MIT-licensed web renderer, r186 (Sept 2026), ~21M weekly npm downloads; glTF-level advanced materials, a subclassable TSL LightingModel for custom BRDFs on WebGPU and WebGL 2, instancing and BatchedMesh, area lights and a TSL post stack; editor tools come from add-ons.
* [Unity](unity.md) - Status NOT CHOSEN. HDRP has fabric, iridescence, anisotropy and ray tracing but is frozen and does not run on iPad; URP runs everywhere but lacks those materials; non-game firms above US$1M pay US$4,950/seat plus about 4% runtime fee; Unity 7 transition under way.
* [Unreal Engine](unreal-engine.md) - Status REJECTED by the owner after a proof of concept; do not re-propose. Unreal 5.8 ships the richest ready-made picture (Substrate fuzz, anisotropy, thin-film, glints; Lumen; path tracer) but glints are not rendered on mobile, editor tools cannot ship in a product, there is no browser runtime, and sold apps owe 5% above US$1M.

# Domain Concept

* [How professional creative tools were built](pro-tool-build-case-studies.md) - Case studies of what comparable tools render with: proprietary engines for narrow deep competencies and tablet-first tools (Procreate, Nomad, Shapr3D, ZBrush, KeyShot), three.js for general 3D editors (Plasticity, Spline v2), game engines (Twinmotion), and DCC layers (JewelCraft on Blender, MatrixGold on Rhino).
